rules.title: Training passport validity
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: present a passport valid on the travel date. An expired sole passport requires denial when no replacement can be obtained.

rules.title: Training visitor permission
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: fictional XZ visitors need a current TRAINING-VISITOR visa with at least one entry remaining, unless an explicitly stated training exception applies. Resolve an available permission inquiry before denial.

rules.title: Training resident exception
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: a current TRAINING-RESIDENT permit may replace a visitor visa. The permit must actually be presented.

rules.title: Training supervisor referral
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: a TRAINING-MANUAL-REVIEW permit whose status cannot be clarified after the offered inquiry requires supervisor escalation. Escalation is not a fallback for other cases.

rules.title: Training connecting journey
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: for the authored SFO–LHR–DUB connection, also request and receive the confirmed onward booking. This is not a statement of actual transit law.

rules.title: Training alternative passports
rules.body: Invented exercise rule: the authored dual-document passenger may present either a current fictional XY passport or a current visitor visa in addition to the initial passport.

rules.title: US citizens travelling by air
rules.body: For the US-citizen visitor cases here, a current US passport supplies travel identification; a Canadian visa and eTA are not required. Other routine acceptance checks are stipulated satisfied.

rules.title: British-citizen and French passports
rules.body: The ordinary British-citizen and French visitor cases in this desk require a current passport and matching valid eTA for air travel, unless the case states another applicable status.

rules.title: eTA and the passport used for travel
rules.body: An eTA is electronic, not a paper boarding document. The airline checks its status against the presented passport. Replacing the passport requires a new matching eTA; an approval tied to a different passport is insufficient.

rules.title: Indian and Chinese visitor passports
rules.body: The ordinary Indian and mainland Chinese visitor cases here require a current passport and valid Canadian visitor visa unless a stated exemption applies. Resolve any offered inquiry about qualifying documents before denying. These nationalities are not in the selected-nationality eTA exception used by some other visa-required travellers.

rules.title: US permanent residents
rules.body: A US lawful permanent resident travelling by air carries a current nationality passport and valid US permanent-resident proof. A current Form I-551 green card is one accepted proof. The visa/eTA visitor requirement does not apply to this status.

rules.title: Canadian permanent residents returning by air
rules.body: For these returning Canadian permanent residents, request a valid PR card with the passport, or a valid permanent resident travel document (PRTD). A visitor visa or eTA does not replace the PR travel evidence.

rules.title: Returning without a PR card
rules.body: An issued, valid PRTD can supply the missing PR travel evidence for a commercial return to Canada. The authored PRTD has one unused entry. Applying for one is different from already possessing it.

rules.title: Study permit and international travel
rules.body: A study permit governs study status; it is not generally a substitute for the required travel visa. For the Indian student who visited Japan as well as the US, an expired visa and current study permit do not establish the US-only return exemption.

rules.title: Returning after visiting only the US
rules.body: The authored returning student already held the current study permit before departure, visited only the US, and returns before the authorized stay ends. IRCC describes a return exception where the visa has expired in these circumstances. Confirm the trip history; the exception does not cover a trip that also included Japan. Border admission remains a separate decision.

rules.title: A travel document is not always a national passport
rules.body: A boarding identity document must be genuine, current and accepted by Canada. IRCC accepts U.S. refugee travel documents (I-571) and re-entry permits (I-327). Issuance by the United States does not make the holder a U.S. citizen. Inspect the document category as well as the issuing country. Air Beluga fictional training procedure: resolve material identity or permission conflicts using the offered checks, then refer unresolved conflicts to a supervisor. This escalation procedure is a game rule, not an IRCC requirement.

rules.title: Canadian visitor permission is separate from a U.S. visa
rules.body: For these Indian and mainland Chinese visitors, a U.S. visitor or work visa does not replace Canadian visitor permission. Check for a Canadian visa or a separately applicable exemption, such as proven U.S. lawful permanent residence.

rules.title: U.S. permanent residents: identity plus status proof
rules.body: A U.S. lawful permanent resident travelling by air needs a valid national passport or accepted equivalent and current accepted proof of U.S. permanent-resident status. A valid Green Card is one such proof. These travellers do not need a Canadian visitor visa or eTA, including holders of Indian or Chinese passports.

rules.title: An expired card calls for supporting status evidence
rules.body: An expired Green Card by itself is not the current status proof listed by IRCC. Check for an accepted extension notice or another listed status document. Card expiry alone is not a determination that permanent-resident status has ended; the puzzle concerns whether sufficient boarding evidence has been presented.

rules.title: U.S. refugee document: visa or a proven exemption
rules.body: A U.S. I-571 refugee travel document is not proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residence. The non-Canadian refugee-document holders in these cases need a Canadian visitor visa unless a separate exemption applies. An eTA is not the substitute for that visa.

rules.title: I-571 and I-327 have different evidence roles
rules.body: For the authored U.S. permanent residents unable to use a national passport, I-571 and I-327 are accepted identity substitutes. I-571 still needs separate permanent-resident proof. IRCC also lists a valid I-327 as accepted status proof, so the same valid I-327 can establish both roles in the authored case.

rules.title: Romania: check whether the passport is electronic
rules.body: Romania’s ordinary visa-exempt air-travel route is limited to electronic passport holders. A non-electronic temporary passport requires a Canadian visitor visa unless another applicable exemption is established. A past eTA email is not Canadian visa evidence.

rules.title: Diplomatic and official do not automatically mean visa-free
rules.body: In these Indian and Chinese visitor cases, diplomatic or official passport classification alone does not remove the Canadian visa requirement. A Canadian diplomatic accreditation or another applicable status exemption must be established separately. A fee exemption for official business is not a travel-permission exemption.
